definitions.short: to stun , i.e. stupefy (with sleep or death)
definitions.usage: (be fast a-, be in a deep, cast into a dead, that) sleep(-er, -eth).
definitions.full: H7290. radam [ רָדַם ] verb Niph`al be in, or fall into, heavy sleep (Late Hebrew id. ; compare Arabic stop up (door, gap, etc.), whence perhaps be deaf (stopped up) to sounds, etc.); — Perfect 3masculine singular נִרְדַּם Judg 4:21 ; 1 singular נִרְדַּמְתִּי Dan 8:8 ; Imperfect 3masculine singular וַיֵּרָדֵם Jonah 1:5 ; Participle נִרְדָּם Prov 10:5 3 t.; — be or fall fast asleep: Judg 4:21 ; Jonah 1:5 (after וַיִּשְׁכַב ), 1:6 (participle, Ges § 120b Da Synt. § 70 (a)); participle as substantive בַּקָּצִיר נִרְדָּם Prov 10:5 ; of sleep of death Psa 76:7 ; stunning effect of awe and dread Dan 8:18 ; 10:9 (both + אָ֑רְצָה [ וּפָנַי ] עַלמָּֿנַי .

occurrences.englishText: Then Jael Heber’s wife took a tent peg, and took a hammer in her hand, and went softly to him, and struck the pin into his temples, and it pierced through into the ground, for he was in a deep sleep; so he fainted and died.
You, even you, are to be feared.
He who gathers in summer is a wise son,
Now as he was speaking with me, I fell into a deep sleep with my face toward the ground; but he touched me, and set me upright.
Yet I heard the voice of his words. When I heard the voice of his words, then I fell into a deep sleep on my face, with my face toward the ground.

Then the mariners were afraid, and every man cried to his god. They threw the cargo that was in the ship into the sea to lighten the ship. But Jonah had gone down into the innermost parts of the ship, and he was laying down, and was fast asleep.
So the ship master came to him, and said to him, “What do you mean, sleeper? Arise, call on your God!† or, gods Maybe your God‡ or, gods will notice us, so that we won’t perish.”
